h1: VEX Ventures — Fintech Hero Section Design
tagline: Hero section reference built around “We back visionaries and craft ventures that define what comes next”, with the layout, timings and palette written down in the brief.
summary: Hero section reference for a fintech product — glass panels, React and Tailwind CSS, Inter and 1000ms transitions.
about: Before rebuilding a hero section for a fintech product, read VEX Ventures: the composition and the specification behind it are both here. The page's own headline reads “We back visionaries and craft ventures that define what comes next”, and the composition is built around those exact words. The page is set in Inter, with the sizes fixed in the brief. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 800x603 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Motion is 1000ms transitions, kept quiet enough that the copy still leads. It is most useful when the Fintech hero section has to survive a copy change without a redesign.

layout.title: Navigation held to one row
layout.body: A slim bar sits over the hero section with the wordmark on the left and the links set in Inter, so the composition reads as content first and chrome second. The bar sits over the 800x603 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: One row, no drawers
layout.body: Focus and hover states are specified for each link rather than inherited from the browser. One action per bar.

layout.title: Measured against the viewport
layout.body: The values are the specification: 18px spacing steps and 1000ms transitions, captured at 800x603 rather than inferred from a screenshot. The type and the layout share the same steps, so nothing drifts when one of them is substituted.

layout.title: Proof in one row
layout.body: The numbers row is the proof: three or four figures on one line, small labels under each, kept in the same Inter as the interface so it reads as data rather than decoration. There are no dividers inside the row; spacing alone separates the figures.

motion.title: Hover where it means something
motion.body: The pointer work is small and specified: hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card, applied to the elements that already look interactive. Hover and focus are specified together, so the pointer and the keyboard get the same information. Keep the interactive layer small.

motion.title: Durations from the brief
motion.body: The controls resolve in 1000ms, fast enough that the page answers as it is touched rather than after it. The same duration is reused across controls, which keeps the interactions feeling like one system.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.weights: Weight not fixed in the brief
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one face for the whole page

notes: Transitions are specified at 1000ms, which is the value to keep when the palette changes.
The reference was captured at 800x603, and every value quoted on this page comes from the same brief.

Transitions are specified at 1000ms, short enough that the page never feels like it is waiting for an animation. Glass surfaces use blur(4px), and the blur is what makes the panels read as material rather than as fill.

customize: Hold the 800x603 frame when you swap the content; the composition was solved against that ratio and a wider export pushes the type off.

editorial.title: How the hero section reflows
editorial.body: Where a template collapses to a single column and hopes, this brief states what happens (the scale is fluid rather than stepped) and keeps the order intact. Autoplay and motion are handled honestly, so the page still communicates when they are unavailable.

editorial.title: Reading VEX Ventures as a spec
editorial.body: Compare this with a template that calls its spacing a preference. Here the same values are named (18px spacing steps and 1000ms transitions), so an edit either keeps them or visibly breaks the composition. Nothing in this hero section depends on a default.

editorial.title: Making the hero section yours
editorial.body: You do not need to rebuild the hero section to make it yours. Replace the headline and the media, keep the scale (18px spacing steps and 1000ms transitions), and the layout still reads as designed. Rewrite the copy and the media before you re-colour anything.

faq.question: What do I get when I copy the VEX Ventures brief?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 800x603, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: Can I rebuild the VEX Ventures hero section in a different stack?
faq.answer: VEX Ventures was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Can I ship a page rebuilt from VEX Ventures without crediting it?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 800x603.
